archetype.name: Playoff Team (Mobley-anchored)
archetype.definition: A sound, above-average team on both ends that should make the playoffs comfortably, carried by an elite frontcourt and Donovan Mitchell, but no longer the overwhelming force its 2024-25 peak suggested.

report.headline: A .500 start hiding a decent team with a Harden problem to solve
report.take:
Cleveland at 5-5 looks like a coin flip, but the sheet describes a team a little better than that. The Net Rtg of 2.8 sits 16th, the offense ranks 11th and the defense 13th, and the margin implies six wins rather than five. The site has the Cavaliers 12th of 30, which fits: an above-average team, not a contender yet, and a slide in quality from the 64-18, 9.5 Net Rtg side of 2024-25 through last year's 4.1. The schedule explains much of the record. Four of the five losses came against Oklahoma City twice, New York and Philadelphia, and the wins include a 136-111 rout at Milwaukee and a 119-95 thumping of the 76ers.

The engine is the frontcourt, graded A-. Evan Mobley ranks 4th among power forwards on the site with a 4.5 BPM and 65.2 TS %, and Jarrett Allen is finishing at a 66.2 TS % when available. Their rim protection is visible in the team numbers: opponents shoot 62 at the rim (6th) and post a 51 eFG % (5th), well under the league's 53.2. Mitchell is the other pillar, 3rd among shooting guards with a 61.6 TS % and a +17.6 On-Off. The offense keeps leaning harder on threes, with a 3PA Rate of 47.1 that is the highest of any season in the sheet, and it protects the ball, posting a 12 TOV % that ranks 4th.

The numbers also show where the drag comes from. James Harden is playing nearly as many minutes as Mitchell, yet his line is a 54.1 TS %, a -1.8 BPM and a -20.2 On-Off, and he ranks 33rd among point guards. Ten games of on-off data is noisy, but every number on his line points the same way. The wings are a C group with nobody healthy who can shoot efficiently: Peyton Watson sits at a 46.5 TS % and Jaylon Tyson is out. On defense the shot-contesting is good, but the Cavaliers force almost nothing, with an Opp TOV % that ranks 29th. That is a big reason a top-five eFG defense grades out only 13th overall.

The direction is better than the 2-3 last five suggests. Over that stretch they outscored opponents by 4.8 a game, up 1.9 on the season figure, and allowed 2.9 fewer points. The November offense dipped to 111 a game after 121 in October, but that stretch included both Thunder games and the Knicks. With Charlotte, Miami and Chicago on the week's slate, this record should start catching up to the margin.

strengths.title: Mobley and Allen own the paint
strengths.body: The A- frontcourt is the best thing on the roster. Mobley is a top-five power forward on the site, and Allen is finishing elite-efficiently. Together they hold opponents to one of the league's lowest rim percentages and a top-five eFG. That is skill-driven rim protection, the same profile as Cleveland's defenses for years, so it should hold as long as Allen's day-to-day status doesn't turn into missed time.

strengths.title: Mitchell drives an efficient offense
strengths.body: Mitchell ranks 3rd among shooting guards and carries a 28.5 USG % at a 61.6 TS %, and the team is far better with him on the floor. Around him the offense hits 36.4 % from three on a heavy volume and turns it over at the league's 4th-lowest rate. That combination is the backbone of an 11th-ranked offense with room to climb back toward last year's 119.2 ORtg.

strengths.title: The margin beats the record
strengths.body: A 2.8 Net Rtg and a positive differential against a schedule heavy on the Thunder and Knicks point to a team playing at a winning level. The margin implies six wins, and the last five games were stronger by point differential than the season as a whole. Some of the .500 record is simply who they played.

concerns.title: Harden's minutes aren't working
concerns.body: Harden plays nearly Mitchell-level minutes but has a sub-par TS %, a negative BPM and the worst On-Off of any regular. Ten games of on-off swings wildly, but every number on his line points the same direction. If his efficiency doesn't recover, the backcourt's B grade is really Mitchell alone.

concerns.title: A thin, inefficient wing group
concerns.body: The wings grade C. Watson is shooting a 46.5 TS %, Tyson is out, and Tristan Enaruna has barely played. Sam Merrill, whose On-Off was strong, is also out, which narrows the shooting around Mitchell. This is a depth problem that health only partly fixes.

concerns.title: No turnovers forced, centers feast
concerns.body: The defense contests shots well but forces turnovers at the second-lowest rate in the league. Opposing centers have also piled up rebounds and points against it. Add a below-average ORB % and Cleveland rarely wins the possession battle, which caps how good a top-five eFG defense can look overall.

trend.note: A 4-2 October gave way to a 1-3 November as the offense cooled against the Thunder and Knicks, but the last five games carried a better margin than the season. The underlying level hasn't moved much; the schedule has.

weekAhead.headline: Three bottom-tier defenses, plus Knicks and Mavericks tests
weekAhead.body:
Five games, the first three on the road. Charlotte, Miami and Chicago are all below .500, and all leak points. Charlotte has the league's worst ORtg and allows opponents a 40.8 3P %. Miami's Opp eFG % ranks last. Chicago, 30th on the site, has the worst DRtg in the league. For a team that takes nearly half its shots from three, those are games to bank, and they're Harden's best chance to get going: Chicago and Miami have both let point guards score well above their own averages.

The Knicks trip is the hard one. New York beat Cleveland 97-109 in Cleveland two days ago, ranks 7th on defense and leads the league in REB %. Dallas arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, after Miami, with the league's best Opp 3P % but a D- backcourt. Four wins is the target. Three would be a missed chance.

keyMatchups.title: The glass at Madison Square Garden
keyMatchups.body: New York is 2nd in ORB % and 1st in REB %, while Cleveland ranks 21st in ORB %. In the loss on Nov. 7 the offense managed only 97 points. Unless Allen is available and Mobley controls the defensive glass, the Knicks will win the possession count again.

keyMatchups.title: Cleveland's threes vs Dallas's perimeter D
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows the lowest 3P % in the league, a direct test of a Cleveland offense built on volume threes. The opening is Mitchell: the Mavericks have let shooting guards score well above their own averages, and their D- backcourt offers little resistance.

keyMatchups.title: Cashing in against Chicago and Charlotte
keyMatchups.body: Chicago's defense is the league's worst, and Charlotte's offense is the league's worst. These are the games where a 12th-ranked team shows it is better than .500. Losing either would say more about Cleveland than about the opponent.

weekAhead.watch: Harden's efficiency against the Chicago and Miami defenses: if he can't score on those, the backcourt question becomes a real one.

restOfSeason.body:
The core is sound. A top-five player at his position in Mobley, Mitchell playing at a top-three shooting-guard level, and an A- frontcourt with real rim protection should keep Cleveland comfortably in the East's playoff group. The current pace of 41 wins understates a team whose margin is already better than its record and whose opening schedule was loaded with the Thunder and Knicks. My range is 44 to 50 wins with a Net Rtg of 2.5 to 5.5. That resembles last season's shape more than the 64-win peak: the offense should drift back up from its November dip, and the defense, already better than last year's 15th, should stay around the top 12.

What won't hold is Harden playing heavy minutes at this level of damage, and something has to give there, either his efficiency recovering or his role shrinking. The thin wing group won't fix itself, and the defense will keep giving up extra possessions until it forces more turnovers. The ceiling is set by whether Allen stays healthy and the backcourt next to Mitchell becomes a plus.
swingFactors: Returns of Merrill and Tyson on the wing

confidence.note: Ten games, a tough opening slate, and noisy on-off splits; the team-level ratings fit the history.
